source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1009 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1009 was established by Ordinance No. 31099, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 23, 2019. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1009 is established on property generally bounded by Cherry Laurel Lane, Sportsmans Parkway, Ridan Lane, and Cavalcade Drive. The size of PD 1009 is approximately 6.226 acres. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered a residential zoning district. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1009A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 1009A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For single family uses, a final plat may serve as the development plan.

(b) For all other uses, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in the district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) An accessory community center (private) is permitted by right and is permitted within a shared access development. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: the yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A- 4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the TH-2(A) Townhouse District apply.

(b) Density. For single family use, maximum number dwelling units is 62.

(c) Height. Maximum structure height is 30 feet. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) For single family uses, two off-street parking spaces are required.

(c) Parking spaces located in an enclosed structure must be at least 20 feet away from the shared access drive or sidewalk if:

(1) the space faces upon the shared access drive or sidewalk; or

(2) the space can be entered directly from the shared access drive. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) A minimum required landscape area equal to 25 percent of the total shared access development area must be provided. Landscape areas in individual lots may be included in the total landscape area measurement.

(c) A 10-foot landscaping buffer with a six-foot high wrought iron fence must be provided along Cherry Laurel Lane and Cavalcade Drive.

(d) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Shared Access Development
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.114. SHARED ACCESS DEVELOPMENT.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, a shared access development must comply with the requirements in Section 51A-4.411.

(b) Individual lots. No more than 62 individual lots may be platted as a shared access

development.

(c) Shared access drives.

(1) Shared access drives must have a minimum paved width of 22 feet.

(2) Shared access drives are required to be striped as fire lanes.

(3) Parking is prohibited on shared access drives.

(d) Sidewalks.

(1) A four-foot-wide sidewalk with a two-foot planting strip between the sidewalk and the shared access drive must be provided adjacent to one side of each shared access drive.

(2) Sidewalks must connect through common areas to provide overall walkability from the dwelling units to the development perimeter and to the community open space.

(e) Guest parking requirements. In addition to any parking spaces required for each dwelling unit, shared access developments must provide 0.50 unassigned spaces available for use by visitors and residents for each dwelling unit. Guest parking spaces must be located where they will not impede access from any other guest parking space or dwelling unit to the shared access point. (Ord. 31099)

SEC. 519-1009.115. COMMUNITY OPEN SPACE.

(a) A minimum of one acre of community open space must be platted as a common area in the location shown on the conceptual plan.

(b) The community open space must be interconnected to the lot areas by walkways, either within the shared access area or adjacent common areas. A walkway must loop through the open space. These walkways must be constructed of a combination of reinforced concrete, brick pavers, decomposed granite, or other suitable materials.

(c) The community open space must be cleared of underbrush and debris, with healthy trees preserved.

(d) Construction activities within the community open pace are limited to walkway construction and required drainage improvements necessary to support the subdivision development.

(e) Community open space must contain the following amenities:

(1) A minimum of two benches;

(2) A minimum of two trash receptacles;

(3) A minimum of two bike racks, for three bicycles each; and

(4) A minimum of one pedestrian street light spaced from 45 feet to 60 feet on center.

(f) A minimum of 10 percent, but not more than 12 percent, of the community open space must be designated as a fenced dog run for off-leash dog activities. The fenced dog run must contain the following amenities:

(1) A minimum of one bench; and

(2) A minimum of one trash receptacle.

(g) The community open space must be enclosed with a perimeter fence and served with landscape irrigation for dedicated planting areas. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31099)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1009.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31099)
